description:
First real export ticket. Take a `ReplaySnapshot` from T-018's segment buffer and produce a single playable MP4 file at the user-requested path via stream-copy (no re-encode) per N-006 happy path. Trim re-encode and max-compat re-encode are slot-reserved but disabled. Audio is deferred.

Scope (binding):
- Implement `replay.save({ durationSeconds })` end-to-end per N-007 §15 + N-005 §15:
  - Inspect the segment buffer; produce a `ReplaySnapshot` whose `segments: SegmentRef[]` covers `durationSeconds` worth of committed segments ending at the most recent committed segment.
  - Pin the snapshot (refcount via T-018).
  - Return the snapshot within 250 ms of the call + remaining fragment encode time (worst case ≈ 2.25 s per N-008 §6).
- Implement `replay.export_start({ snapshot, options })` per N-006:
  - Emit `export.queued` immediately.
  - Plan the export: for the MVP, every snapshot is assumed to be a contiguous H.264 stream with consistent format → `mode: "stream-copy"`. Emit `export.started { mode, plan, estDurationS, estOutputBytes }`.
  - Stream-copy path:
    - Build an MP4 with a single shared `moov` containing the sample table for all snapshot segments. The simplest correct implementation is to invoke `ffmpeg -i 'concat:seg0.mp4|seg1.mp4|...' -c copy -movflags +faststart out.mp4` per N-006. Alternative: in-process remux using `mp4-rust` or similar. Either is acceptable; document the choice.
    - faststart placement is mandatory per N-008 §6 (moov before mdat).
    - Re-encoding is NOT in MVP scope. If the segments cannot be stream-copied (format change, missing IDR at start), emit `export.failed { reasonCode: "stream-copy-requires-reencode" }` with a `diagnosticsPath` and stop. T-019a (follow-up) implements the lead-trim re-encode and discontinuity re-encode paths.
  - Emit `export.progress` at 1 Hz with `stage`, `pct`, `bytesIn`, `bytesOut`, `etaMs`.
  - On completion: stat the output file, compute SHA-256, emit `export.completed { exportId, finalPath, bytes, sha256, durationS, mode, fpsObservedOut }`.
  - On failure: emit `export.failed { exportId, stage, reasonCode, details, diagnosticsPath }`. Reason codes per N-007 §17 (`ffmpeg-spawn-failed`, `ffmpeg-exited-nonzero`, `stream-copy-requires-reencode`, etc.).
  - Exactly-once terminal event invariant per N-008 §6.7: each `exportId` produces exactly one of `completed | failed | cancelled | rejected`.
- Implement `replay.export_cancel({ exportId })`:
  - If the export is still in `QUEUED` or `COPY` stage → cancel cleanly, emit `export.cancelled { stage, partialBytes }`.
  - If the export has reached `MUXING` stage → reject the cancel; the existing terminal event will still fire. Per N-007 §15.
- Implement `replay.restore_recovered_session({ sessionId })`:
  - Adopts a recovered session from T-018's recovery scan and returns a `ReplaySnapshot` over its segments. Export proceeds normally.
  - `replay.discard_recovered_session({ sessionId })` removes the segments directory.
- Mid-export reaping: if a prior helper run died mid-export, its partially-written output file under the export staging dir is reaped at boot (before `engine.ready`) per N-008 §6.10.
- Concurrent recording during export: capture frame production MUST continue at within 2× the pre-export drop baseline (N-008 §6.7). The export path runs on its own thread; the encoder/segment writers are untouched.
- ffmpeg path: shipped as a static binary alongside the helper, OR resolved from `PATH` with a probe at boot. Implementer's choice; default = resolve from `PATH` and probe at boot; emit `helper-unavailable` with `ffmpeg-missing` if not found. T-010d handles packaging.

Out of scope (binding):
- No trim-head re-encode, no discontinuity re-encode, no max-compat re-encode (follow-up T-019a if needed for T-021 smoke).
- No HEVC, no AV1, no 10-bit export.
- No audio track in the output (single video track only).
- No multi-snapshot batching.
- No tests on M2/M3/M4 — T-010c.

Acceptance criteria:
1. After 60 s of capture on M1, `replay.save({durationSeconds: 30})` returns a `ReplaySnapshot` within 2.5 s wall time; subsequent `replay.export_start` produces a playable `out.mp4` within 5 s wall time.
2. `ffprobe out.mp4` reports `duration ≈ 30 s ± 1 frame`, `codec h264`, `IsStreamable=Yes` (mediainfo) or moov-before-mdat (ffprobe).
3. The output frame count equals `round(30 × declared_fps) ± 1` per N-008 §6.3. No fake duplicated frames.
4. `export.progress` events fire at ~1 Hz with monotonically increasing `pct`.
5. Cancelling the export during `COPY` stage produces `export.cancelled`; cancelling during `MUXING` is refused but the existing `completed`/`failed` terminal event still fires.
6. Killing the helper mid-export and relaunching reaps the orphaned partial output file before `engine.ready` per N-008 §6.10.
7. Concurrent recording continues during export: `capture.diagnostics.dropped_since_last` stays within 2× the pre-export baseline.
8. Exactly one terminal event per `exportId` (no duplicate `completed`+`failed`, no missing terminals).
9. `--simulate` mode from T-015 still works.

Verification commands:
- `cargo build -p cove-replay-engine`
- `cargo test -p cove-replay-engine`
- Manual on M1: 60 s capture + 30 s replay save + export; play the output in VLC/mpv.
- `ffprobe -show_format -show_streams out.mp4`
- `mediainfo out.mp4 | grep IsStreamable`
- Cancel-during-COPY and cancel-during-MUXING manual tests.
- SIGKILL-mid-export then relaunch and inspect export staging dir.
- `git status --short`

Codex review expectations:
- Confirm faststart placement (moov before mdat) on the output.
- Confirm exactly-one terminal event per exportId (N-008 §6.7).
- Confirm cancel semantics: cancellable through `COPY`, refused at `MUXING`.
- Confirm mid-export orphan reaping happens before `engine.ready` (N-008 §6.10).
- Confirm concurrent recording is not stalled by export (no shared mutex on the capture/encoder hot path).
- Confirm Linux re-encode (when later added) is libx264-only per N-008 §6.8 — verify the current code path does not call any other CPU encoder.
- Flag any path traversal in `finalPath` handling.
- Flag any silent fallback from stream-copy to re-encode — the design requires `stream-copy-requires-reencode` rather than transparent re-encoding for the MVP.

Failure handling:
- If two attempts to land the stream-copy path produce non-playable output, hand the ticket back per WORKFLOW.md "Failed fix reset". Do not switch to re-encode silently — that breaks the v1.1.0 ceiling proof.

No commits, tags, or publishes from this ticket.
title: Implement replay snapshot + export/remux MVP (stream-copy)
